# Turn a messy email into a clear bullet-point list with Hugging Face’s free summarizer


You’ve just opened an email that’s three paragraphs long and full of extra details. Instead of reading it twice, paste it into Hugging Face’s free summarizer and get a clean bullet-point list in seconds—ready to copy into your notes or share with your team.

## Before you start
- A free Hugging Face account ([sign up here](https://huggingface.co/join))
- A web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, or Safari)
- Any email text you want to simplify (copy it to your clipboard)
- 5 minutes total time

---

## Step 1 — Go to Hugging Face’s summarizer demo
Open your browser and go to [https://huggingface.co/spaces/facebook/bart-large-cnn](https://huggingface.co/spaces/facebook/bart-large-cnn). You’ll see a clean page with a large text box and a “Generate” button below it. This page is called a “Space” — it’s like a mini web app that runs the summarizer for you.

You’ll know it worked when the page loads and you see the big text box ready for you to paste your email.

💬 Example:
Just visit the link above in your browser.

---

## Step 2 — Paste your email into the text box
Click inside the large text box. A blinking cursor will appear. Press **Ctrl+V** (Windows/Linux) or **Cmd+V** (Mac) to paste your email text. If you’re on a phone, long-press the box and choose “Paste.” The text will appear in the box, and the word count will update below it.

You’ll know it worked when you see your email text inside the box and the word count changes from “0 words” to the actual number of words in your email.

💬 Example:
Paste this short email:
> Hi team,
> The quarterly budget review meeting is scheduled for next Tuesday at 2pm in Conference Room B. Please bring your department’s updated forecasts and any questions about the new expense policy. If you can’t attend, let me know by Monday 5pm so we can reschedule. Thanks!

---

## Step 3 — Click “Generate” to create the summary
Below the text box, look for a blue button labeled **Generate**. Click it once. The button will change to “Generating…” and a progress bar may appear. Wait a few seconds — the AI will read your email and write a shorter version.

You’ll know it worked when the button changes back to **Generate** and a new box appears below with your bullet-point list.

💬 Example:
Click the blue “Generate” button.

---

## Step 4 — Read the bullet-point list in the output box
A new box will appear under the button. It will show your email rewritten as short bullet points. Each point is a key idea from the original email. If the list feels too long or too short, you can edit it directly in the box.

You’ll know it worked when you see a clean list of bullet points that capture the main ideas of your email.

💬 Example:
The output might look like:
- Quarterly budget review meeting scheduled for next Tuesday at 2pm in Conference Room B
- Bring department forecasts and questions about the new expense policy
- RSVP by Monday 5pm if you can’t attend

---

## Step 5 — Copy the bullet points to use anywhere
Click inside the output box. Press **Ctrl+A** then **Ctrl+C** (Windows/Linux) or **Cmd+A** then **Cmd+C** (Mac) to select all the text and copy it. If you’re on a phone, long-press the text and choose “Select all,” then “Copy.” Now you can paste the bullet points into a document, chat, or note-taking app.

You’ll know it worked when you can paste the bullet points into another app and they appear exactly as you copied them.

💬 Example:
Press Ctrl+A, then Ctrl+C (or the phone equivalents) to copy the bullet points.

---

## Common mistakes
- **Pasting too much text**: The summarizer works best with emails under 1,000 words. If your email is longer, split it into two parts and summarize each separately.
- **Not clicking Generate**: The AI won’t start until you click the button. If nothing happens, double-check you clicked “Generate.”
- **Editing the output too early**: Wait until the bullet points appear before you edit them. If you edit while it’s still generating, your changes may be lost.

---

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life**: Next time you get a long email from a colleague or client, paste it into the summarizer and get a clean list you can forward or add to your to-do list.
- **For your business or work**: Use the summarizer to turn long meeting notes or client requests into quick bullet points you can share in a chat or email without losing the main ideas.
- **If you're just getting started**: Start with a short email (under 100 words) to see how the summarizer works. Once you’re comfortable, try longer ones.

---

## Try it now
Open your browser, go to [https://huggingface.co/spaces/facebook/bart-large-cnn](https://huggingface.co/spaces/facebook/bart-large-cnn), paste this short email, click “Generate,” and copy the bullet points into a note. You’ll have a clean list in under a minute.
